data.long_meaning: Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector in Jericho, who, when he heard that Jesus of Nazareth had come to the city, made an effort to see him in spite of his short stature. Jesus, seeing him, invited himself to Zacchaeus' house, and while there he healed the man of his infirmity and promised him salvation. The name Zacchel carries the meaning “God remembers” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Zacchel usually hope their child will grow to embody god remembers and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Zacchaeus is synonymous with undeserving yet repentant tax collectors who sought forgiveness and redemption. In a broader sense, it can represent the idea of the transformative power of faith and repentance, as well as the importance of individual action and personal responsibility in becoming a better and more virtuous person.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Zacchaeus carries a deep spiritual significance as it illustrates the power of forgiveness and the importance of turning towards God for salvation and redemption. It also emphasizes the importance of personal transformation through penance and repentance. The story of Zacchaeus serves as an example of how even those who have strayed far from the path of righteousness can return to God and find salvation.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, sought to see Jesus and regained his lost honor through repentance and restitution. His name symbolizes transformation from a corrupt collector to a righteous man in God's eyes.

historical_references.reference: Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector and a wealthy man in Jericho. He was short in stature and a great crowd had gathered in front of him to see Jesus, but he could not see over their heads. So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to catch a glimpse of Jesus as He passed by. Jesus looked up at him and said, 'Zacchaeus, hurry and come down. I must stay at your house today.' Zacchaeus was overjoyed to receive such a visit and hurried down. All who saw this were put in an uproar and grumbled, saying, 'He went to be a guest with a sinful man.' But Zacchaeus responded, 'I will give half of my possessions to the poor, and if I have cheated anyone of anything, I will pay back four times the amount.'
historical_references.context: The New Testament of the Bible, Luke 19:1-10

historical_references.reference: The name 'Zacchaeus' is derived from the Hebrew name 'Zakkai', which means 'pure' or 'righteous'. However, the New Testament uses the Greek form, 'Zacchaeus'. The tax collectors in Judea during this period were notorious for their extortionate practices and were considered social outcasts by the Jewish population. Despite his wealth and status as a chief tax collector, Zacchaeus' encounter with Jesus led him to repent and make amends for his dishonest practices.
historical_references.context: The New Testament of the Bible, Luke 19:1-10

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Zacchaeus is now commonly associated with individuals who have undergone a significant transformation in their lives, particularly in the areas of finance, entrepreneurship, and philanthropy. This modern context is derived from the biblical character Zacchaeus, a tax collector who, upon encountering Jesus, was moved to make amends for his past wrongs and gave half of his wealth to the poor. Today, people with the name Zacchaeus or similar variations are often found in professional networking sites like LinkedIn, where they share stories of success and redemption. They are also active on Twitter, using the platform to engage in dialogues about business and philanthropy. Additionally, some Zacchaeus individuals write for blogs or publications on Medium, sharing their experiences and insights with wider audiences.
